questions.question: A book with a marked price of ₹ 600 is available at a discount of 18%. What is the discount given?
questions.questionHtml: A book with a marked price of ₹ 600 is available at a discount of 18%. What is the discount given?
questions.solution:
Given:

A book with a marked price of ₹ 600 is available at a discount of 18%. 

Formula used:

Discount value = \(\frac{\text{discount percent}}{100}\times \text{marked price}\) 

Calculation:

Discount value = \(\frac{18}{100}\times 600 = 108\) 

∴The discount given on the book is Rs. 108.

Now,  Discount% = \(1,500\over 15,000\) × 100 = 10%.

questions.question: A cell phone was marked at 20% above the cost price and discount of 10% was given on its marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.questionHtml: A cell phone was marked at 20% above the cost price and discount of 10% was given on its marked price. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
Let CP of cell phone was be Rs. 100

MP of the cell phone = 100 × 120/100 = 120

SP of the cell phone = 120 × 90/100 = 108

∴ Profit = 108 - 100 = 8

Profit % = 8/100 × 100 = 8%

Short Trick :

Profit % = 20 - 10 - (20 × 10)/100 = 10 - 2 = 8%

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at a price 20% higher than their cost price and allows 10% discount on every item. Find his gain percentage.

Let, the cost price = 100

The marked price = 100 + (20% of 100) = 100 + 20 = 120

The selling price = 120 - (10% of 120) = 120 - 12 = 108

The gain percentage = 108 - 100 = 8%

questions.question: A man buys an article for Rs. 3,200 and sells it at a loss of 12%. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.questionHtml: A man buys an article for Rs. 3,200 and sells it at a loss of 12%. What is the selling price of the article?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

A loss of 12% means the Selling Price (SP) is 88% of the Cost Price (CP).

SP = CP × 0.88

SP = 3200 × 0.88

SP = 32 × 88 = ₹2,816.

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,816.

Alternate Method

Given: Cost Price (CP) = ₹3,200 and Loss Percentage = 12%.

Formula: Selling Price (SP) = CP − Loss

⇒ Loss Amount = 12% of 3200

⇒ Loss Amount = (12/100) × 3200

⇒ Loss Amount = 12 × 32 = ₹384.

⇒ SP = CP − Loss Amount

⇒ SP = 3200 − 384 = ₹2,816.

⇒ Comparing with the given options, the result corresponds to Option (2).

∴ The correct answer is ₹2,816.

Additional Information

Selling Price for Profit

When there is a profit, SP = CP × (100 + Profit %)/100.

Finding Cost Price

To find CP when SP and loss are known: CP = (SP × 100) / (100 − Loss %).

Profit/Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss percentage is always calculated on the Cost Price unless specified otherwise.

questions.question: Kuldeep offers his customers a discount of 10% on the marked price of a suitcase and he still makes a profit of 20%. What is the actual cost of the suitcase marked for Rs 2,500?
questions.questionHtml: Kuldeep offers his customers a discount of 10% on the marked price of a suitcase and he still makes a profit of 20%. What is the actual cost of the suitcase marked for Rs 2,500?
questions.solution:
SP of suitcase = MP – Discount % of MP

SP = 2500 – 10% of 2500 = \(2500-\frac{10}{100}\times 2500\) = Rs. 2250

So, CP of suitcase = \(\frac{100}{100+20}\times 2250\) = \(\frac{100}{120}\times 2250\) = Rs. 1875

questions.question: The printed price on a book is Rs. 150. If it is sold after two successive discounts of 30% and 40%, then find its selling price.
questions.questionHtml: The printed price on a book is Rs. 150. If it is sold after two successive discounts of 30% and 40%, then find its selling price.
questions.solution:
Given

Marked price of book = Rs. 150

1st discount = 30%

2nd discount = 40%

Formula used:

Discount = Marked price – Selling price

Discount % = Discount/Marked price × 100

When 2 discounts are given,

Net discount = (D1 + D2 – D1D2/100)%

Where, D1 = Discount 1

D2 = Discount 2

Calculation:

Net discount = (D1 + D2 – D1D2/100)%

Net Discount = [30 + 40 – (30)(40)/100]%

⇒ Net Discount = (70 – 12)

⇒ Net Discount = 58% 

Discount % = Discount/Marked price × 100

⇒ 58% = Discount/150 × 100

⇒ Discount = 58 × 150/100 = 87 

Discount = Marked price – Selling price

⇒ 87 = 150 – Selling price

⇒ Selling Price = Rs. 63

∴ Its selling price is Rs. 63  

Shortcut Trick 

Discount fraction MP SP

40% (-4/10) 10 6


⇒Discount = 100 - 42 = 58  

⇒ D% = (58/100) × 100 = 58%

as per the question,

SP = 150 - (150 × 58)/100 = 63

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows 40% discount on his goods. He further gives 20% discount. What is the single discount equivalent to these two successive discounts?
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper allows 40% discount on his goods. He further gives 20% discount. What is the single discount equivalent to these two successive discounts?
questions.solution:
Single equivalent discount formula for successive discounts: \(D = A + B - \left(\frac{A \times B}{100}\right)\)

Let A = 40% and B = 20%.

⇒ D = A + B − (A × B ÷ 100)

⇒ D = 40 + 20 − (40 × 20 ÷ 100) = 60 − 8 = 52%

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked the price 20% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 30%, then find his loss percent.
questions.questionHtml: A shopkeeper marked the price 20% more than its cost price. If he allows a discount of 30%, then find his loss percent.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

We can use the successive percentage change formula: Net % Change = a + b + (a × b) / 100

Here, the markup percentage (a) = +20% and the discount percentage (b) = −30%.

Net % Change = 20 − 30 + (20 × −30) / 100

Net % Change = −10 − 6 = −16%

The negative sign indicates an overall loss of 16%.

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Alternate Method

Given:

⇒ Markup Percentage = 20%

⇒ Discount Percentage = 30%

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = CP + 20% of CP = 100 + 20 = 120

⇒ Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP − 30% of MP

⇒ SP = 120 − (30 / 100 × 120) = 120 − 36 = 84

⇒ Since Selling Price is less than Cost Price, there is a loss.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 84 = 16

⇒ Loss Percentage = (Loss / CP) × 100 = (16 / 100) × 100 = 16%

∴ The correct answer is 16%.

Additional Information

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, the single equivalent discount is calculated as: D = a + b − (a × b) / 100.

CP and MP Relationship

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by the formula: CP / MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%). If there is a loss, use (100 − Loss%).

Dishonest Dealer Rule

When a shopkeeper claims to sell goods at Cost Price but uses a false weight, the actual profit percent is: Profit% = (Error / True Weight − Error) × 100.

questions.question: What is the selling price of a dress that has a marked price of Rs. 500 and is given a 20% discount and subsequently a 10% discount?

SP of dress after 10% discount = 400 – 400 × \(\frac{10}{100}\) = 400 – 40 = 360
